definition: Laboratory robotics is the act of using robots in biology, chemistry or engineering labs.
details: For example, pharmaceutical companies employ robots to move biological or chemical samples around to synthesize novel chemical entities or to test pharmaceutical value of existing chemical matter. Advanced laboratory robotics can be used to completely automate the process of science, as in the Robot Scientist project. Laboratory processes are suited for robotic automation as the processes are composed of repetitive movements (e.g., pick/place, liquid/solid additions, heating/cooling, mixing, shaking, and testing). Many laboratory robots are commonly referred as autosamplers, as their main task is to provide continuous samples for analytical devices.

explainer.lead: Laboratory robotics uses robots in biology, chemistry or engineering labs. It matters because lab processes consist of repetitive movements well suited to automation, and it can even automate the process of science.

tiers.eli5: It is using robot arms and machines to do the boring, repeated bench work, like moving tubes and mixing liquids, so scientists can focus on thinking.
tiers.practitioner: Pharma companies deploy robots to move samples for chemical synthesis or testing. A pitfall is that only processes built from repeatable pick/place, liquid/solid addition, heating/cooling and mixing steps automate cleanly.
tiers.paperLevel: Laboratory robotics applies robots to lab workflows; advanced systems can fully automate scientific experimentation, as in the Robot Scientist project. Suitability derives from the repetitive, procedural nature of lab movements.

explainer.example: A pharmaceutical company uses robots to shuttle biological and chemical samples between stations to synthesize novel compounds and test existing ones.
